discovery.rule: Never hard-code the active project set in an operator prompt. Load enabled projects from the portfolio registry on every cycle.

execution.nextUsefulStateRule: After each verified integration, infer the next user-meaningful bottleneck or missing journey and immediately discover/plan safe work toward that state without waiting for the operator to name the next task.
execution.testabilityRule: When enough capabilities exist for meaningful human use, prioritize making the product runnable, observable and testable by the user before accumulating lower-value isolated features.

generationRule: A generation advances only when new real work is produced or verified: code, capability, bug fix, UX, integration, functional test, performance, resilience, security or another concrete product improvement. Administrative ref/checkpoint churn alone is not a generation.
autonomyRule: The operator supplies goals, priorities and human-gate decisions. RAZZO owns routine project-management reasoning: identify the next useful state, expose bottlenecks, create safe workstreams, execute, verify, integrate and replan continuously. Do not wait for the operator to enumerate obvious next steps.
onboardingRule: A new project joins RAZZO by adding one enabled entry to razzo/projects.json. The universal operator command and scheduled tasks must not be edited for project onboarding.
